title: Stanford Evo 2 AI model generates phages against E. coli
slides: Can one AI model outsmart E. coli?
Stanford's Evo 2 designs phages from scratch
It succeeds where evolutionary biology failed
Your lab could now generate custom viruses
Test Evo 2 on your resistant strain today
thread_text:
1. E. coli's worst nightmare?

Stanford's Evo 2 just designed a phage from scratch—something evolution couldn't do in 4 billion years.

2. Evolution's failure is now AI's win

Natural phages can't keep up with resistant bacteria, but Evo 2 generates new viruses in hours.

3. Custom viruses on demand

Your lab could soon design phages for any resistant strain—no more waiting for nature to catch up.

4. The twist: it works

The AI doesn't just imitate—it outperforms natural evolution, creating phages that kill where traditional ones fail.

5. Test it on your strain today

Got a resistant bug? Upload its genome to Evo 2 and see if it designs a match. What's stopping you?

instagram.caption:
A bacteria strain that shrugs off every known phage just met its match: Stanford's Evo 2 model designed a custom virus from scratch that kills E. coli—something natural evolution hasn't managed in 4 billion years. 🦠

Evo 2 doesn't tweak existing phages—it builds entirely new ones in hours, targeting the exact genetic weak spot of your resistant strain. Labs that were stuck with dead-end treatments now have a design tool for instant, bespoke viruses.

For anyone running a lab: you can upload a resistant strain's genome and get a working phage candidate back—no waiting for nature to catch up.

What's the most antibiotic-resistant bug you're fighting right now—and have you checked if Evo 2 can crack it? 🔬
